what_this_is: The cross-domain doors that are OPEN on the line today. Every entry is a violation of the rule
gate:domain-doors enforces (ADR-0037), keyed on (path, door) — the FILE and the ENV-KEY NAME —
and every entry names the ruling that will close it. `line` is INFORMATIONAL: a line number is a
coordinate, not an identity, and keying on one made an unrelated PR that inserted four lines above
a door read as both a new violation and a stale entry. Refresh the informational lines with
The list exists so the gate is GREEN on the tip on the day it lands and RED the moment a NEW
undeclared door appears — a gate that starts red is a gate nobody runs. It is checked in BOTH
directions AND BY COUNT: N entries for a (path, door) excuse exactly N violations, so a new door
of the same name in the same file turns the gate red, a removed one leaves a surplus entry and
turns it red too, and the list can neither rot into a permanent exemption nor outlive the code it
This list shrinking IS the migration backlog. The only correct direction for it is shorter.

PRD decision 40.5. HALF CLOSED: the URL now defaults to the gateway's assembled MCP surface (deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml, VEXA_MCP_URL) and `core/agent/worker` is classed `client` in this script's own UNITS (its VEXA_MCP_URL sites no longer appear above — client→edge is allowed outright). What remains open is THIS file: it is `agent` control-plane/shared code, not the worker, so it stays domain-kind and a domain may never name the mcp edge directly (the rule has no capability-class escape for domain→edge, unlike domain→domain). The entry closes when dispatch.py mints the worker's env from a value it does not itself hold as a literal MCP_URL/VEXA_MCP_URL-shaped key — e.g. the worker's own default (now in compose) covers the no-override case and this code only ever forwards an explicit operator override, or the mint moves into a helper this script does not scan as `agent`.

This is NOT the ADR-0037 seam (that one closed: `core/agent/worker` is now classed `client`, and its VEXA_MCP_URL sites are an ordinary client→edge reach, allowed outright). This is the worker reporting friction back to the SAME agent-api that spawned it — a callback to its own domain, not a client reaching an unrelated one — using an already-declared, already-defaulted config key (`VEXA_AGENT_API_SELF_URL`, config.v1.json class `defaulted`). The entry closes when the worker files friction through the assembled MCP edge (`report_friction`, already in `core/flows/mcp.tools.v1.json`) instead of calling agent-api's `/api/friction` directly, or when a worker-owned callback door is given its own declared class.

PRD decision 40.7 and decision 5 (flows → meetings, 12 call sites via the gateway; architecture pass §1). THE CAPABILITY DECLARATION HAS LANDED and this entry did NOT close with it — the previous ruling promised it would, and the checker cannot honour that. VEXA_FLOWS_GATEWAY_URL is now class 'capability' with a declared degrade (flows_config.py, config.v1.json capability 'meetings'), and eight production steps answer meetings:not_present — but judge() refuses a DOMAIN naming an EDGE unconditionally, before it ever looks at the class: the capability escape hatch is a domain→domain rule, and doorOwner() resolves this key to the gateway. THE ENTRY CLOSES ON THE DE-HOP, not on a class. And the de-hop is not a rename: the gateway resolves the caller's key and enriches every forward with X-User-Id, X-User-Scopes, X-User-Workspaces and X-User-Limits, and meeting-api's POST /bots derives the per-user concurrent-bot cap from the last of those (core/meetings/services/meeting-api/src/meeting_api/bot_spawn/router.py:208 _resolve_max_concurrent). Calling meeting-api directly without carrying those forward drops the cap silently, so this entry closes only when that enrichment has a home.

PRD decision 46 — clients reach ONE edge with a bearer. The SECOND door of this name in this file, and the same door as the mint below it: Vexa-ai/vexa#1591 made the first-visit arrival conditional on whether the person has anything to return to, and that question is internal-tier for the same reason minting is — it answers about somebody else's account from an address alone, over X-Internal-Secret, which a browser holds no equivalent of. Routing the guard through the gateway while the call it guards goes direct would be two answers to one question. The entry closes with its sibling, when the terminal's auth routes are bound in routes.v1 and the client reads only GATEWAY_URL.
